lessons.title: Four Gospels, one Christ
lessons.idea: The four Gospels are the heart of Scripture. They are historical and faith-filled.
lessons.question: Why four Gospels?
lessons.activity: Compare the four Gospels in a chart.
teach: The Gospels are the heart of Scripture because they are our principal source for the life and teaching of the Incarnate Word (CCC 125). Each has an audience and emphasis: Matthew (Jewish Christians), Mark (Roman, action), Luke (Gentiles, mercy), John (theological).
They were written after oral preaching, in three stages: Jesus’ life and teaching, apostolic preaching, written Gospels (Dei Verbum 19; CCC 126).
Activity: compare the Gospels on the Beatitudes/Sermon on the Plain.
talk: Why four Gospels instead of one?
How do we know they are reliable?
quiz: The Gospels are…|Fiction|Our principal source for the life of Christ|Poetry|Commentary|1|CCC 125.
The first Gospel written is generally held to be…|John|Luke|Matthew|Mark|3|Tradition.
The Gospels were formed from…|Dreams|Later councils|Myth|Oral tradition and eyewitnesses|3|CCC 126.
lessons.life: Read the first chapter of each Gospel over four days.
lessons.saint: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John: the four evangelists, who handed on the good news of Jesus.

lessons.title: How the Gospels were formed
lessons.idea: Jesus’ life, oral tradition, writing.
lessons.question: What stages shaped the Gospels?
teach: Three stages: Jesus’s ministry, oral preaching, writing (CCC 126). Evangelists selected, arranged and adapted for their communities but remained faithful to the truth.
Dates: Mark c. 65–70; Matthew and Luke c. 70–85; John c. 90–100.
talk: Why were the Gospels written down?
quiz: Luke wrote his Gospel after…|Dreaming|Investigating from the beginning|Reading Mark only|Losing his notes|1|Luke 1:3.
The Gospels reflect…|Eyewitness tradition|Rumor|Pure invention|Greek myth|0|Dei Verbum 19.
John’s Gospel is…|A genealogy|A chronicle|Highly theological|A law code|2|CCC 125.
lessons.life: Read Luke 1:1–4 and note what Luke says about method.
lessons.saint: Luke: the physician and evangelist.

lessons.title: Reading the Gospels well
lessons.idea: Read in context with prayer and the Church.
lessons.question: What are the three criteria for interpretation?
lessons.activity: Study a Gospel passage using them.
teach: Three criteria for reading (CCC 112–114): unity of Scripture, living Tradition, analogy of faith.
talk: What is the analogy of faith?
quiz: The analogy of faith is…|A parable|The coherence of the truths of faith|A comparison|A hymn|1|CCC 114.
The Church reads Scripture in light of…|The news|Tradition|Rumor|Opinion only|1|CCC 113.
Which is NOT a criterion?|Private mood|Tradition|Analogy of faith|Unity of Scripture|0|CCC 112-114.
lessons.life: Apply the three criteria to one passage.
lessons.saint: Ambrose: bishop of Milan, who taught Augustine and wrote on the sacraments.

lessons.title: The Word became flesh
lessons.idea: Jesus is true God and true man.
lessons.question: What does the Incarnation show?
lessons.activity: Explain it in a short talk.
teach: The Word became flesh (John 1:14; CCC 461–463). Jesus is true God and true man, one Person with two natures (CCC 464–469).
Chalcedon (451): without confusion, change, division, or separation.
talk: What does the Incarnation show about matter and the body?
Which heresy denies his humanity? His divinity?
quiz: The Incarnation is…|A parable|A metaphor|God becoming man|Man becoming God|2|CCC 461.
Docetism denied…|His birth|His death|Christ’s real humanity|His divinity|2|CCC 465.
Chalcedon taught…|One nature|Two natures in one Person|No Person|Two Persons|1|CCC 467.
lessons.life: Pray John 1:1–14 slowly.
lessons.saint: Athanasius: bishop of Alexandria, who defended the divinity of Christ through repeated exiles.

lessons.title: Annunciation and birth
lessons.idea: Mary says yes. Jesus is born.
lessons.question: What do we learn from the infancy accounts?
teach: The infancy narratives (Mt 1–2; Lk 1–2) reveal Jesus’s identity (CCC 496–507; 525–530).
Compare Matthew and Luke: both agree on virginal conception, Bethlehem, Nazareth.
talk: What do the narratives say about who Jesus is?
quiz: Mary conceived by…|An angel|A prophet|Joseph|The Holy Spirit|3|Luke 1:35.
Jesus was born in…|Nazareth|Cana|Bethlehem|Rome|2|Luke 2:4-7.
Matthew emphasizes…|The shepherds|Mary’s Magnificat|The census only|Fulfilment of prophecy|3|Matthew 1-2.
lessons.life: Read Matthew 1–2 and Luke 1–2 in a week.
lessons.saint: Joseph: the quiet carpenter who protected Mary and Jesus and trusted God’s word in dreams.

lessons.title: The hidden life
lessons.idea: Jesus lived in Nazareth for thirty years.
lessons.question: Why was it hidden?
teach: The hidden life (CCC 531–534): thirty years of ordinary life sanctify ordinary life. Jesus obeys, works, prays.
talk: How does it sanctify our daily life?
How do you honor your parents?
quiz: Jesus lived in Nazareth for about…|Thirty years|One year|Three years|Ten years|0|CCC 534.
At twelve he was found in…|Capernaum|Egypt|Cana|The Temple|3|Luke 2:46.
He was subject to…|The king|The priests|No one|Mary and Joseph|3|Luke 2:51.
lessons.life: Offer your ordinary tasks to God.
lessons.saint: Joseph the carpenter: a worker who taught Jesus a trade and showed that ordinary work can be holy.

units.title: The public ministry
units.eq: What did Jesus teach and do?

lessons.title: Baptism and temptation
lessons.idea: Jesus begins his ministry.
lessons.question: What does the baptism of Jesus show?
lessons.activity: Trace the movement of the Spirit.
teach: Jesus’s baptism (Mt 3:13–17) reveals the Trinity; the temptation (Mt 4:1–11) shows him as the new Adam and new Israel (CCC 535–540).
Compare with Israel in the desert: 40 years vs 40 days.
talk: How do the temptations parallel Israel?
quiz: At the baptism the Spirit descended as…|A star|A flame|A cloud|A dove|3|Matthew 3:16.
Jesus fasted…|Seven days|Three days|Ten days|Forty days|3|Matthew 4:2.
He answered temptation with…|Anger|Scripture|Silence|Magic|1|Matthew 4:4.
lessons.life: Memorize one Scripture to use against temptation.
lessons.saint: Antony of the Desert: the father of monks, who went into the desert to pray and fight temptation.

lessons.title: The Kingdom and parables
lessons.idea: Jesus proclaims God’s reign.
lessons.question: Why parables?
teach: Parables reveal and conceal (Mt 13:10–17). Key parables: sower, mustard seed, leaven, treasure, pearl, net, lost sheep, prodigal son.
The Kingdom is present and coming (CCC 541–546).
quiz: The Kingdom of God is…|A territory|God’s reign begun in Christ|A party|A building|1|CCC 541.
The parable of the sower shows…|Politics|Economics|Farming tips|Different responses to the word|3|Mark 4.
Jesus told parables to…|Reveal truths to those open|Hide from soldiers|Make money|Confuse everyone|0|Matthew 13.
lessons.life: Read a parable each day for a week.
lessons.saint: Francis: who gave up wealth to follow Christ in poverty and joy and loved creation.

lessons.title: Miracles as signs
lessons.idea: Miracles show the Kingdom has come.
lessons.question: What do miracles signify?
teach: Miracles as signs (CCC 547–550): they accompany his word and call to faith; they are not magic.
talk: Why does Jesus often ask for faith?
quiz: Miracles are…|Signs of the Kingdom|Tricks|Legends|Natural events|0|CCC 547.
The first sign in John is…|Raising Lazarus|Feeding|Cana|Walking on water|2|John 2:11.
Jesus often asks for…|Silence|Faith|Money|Fasting|1|Mark 5:34.
lessons.life: List the miracles of Mark 1–5.
lessons.saint: Padre Pio: a Capuchin friar known for hours in the confessional and for his devotion to the Mass.

units.title: The Sermon on the Mount
units.eq: How does Jesus teach us to live?

lessons.title: The Beatitudes
lessons.idea: The way to happiness.
lessons.question: Why “blessed”?
teach: The Beatitudes (Mt 5:3–12; CCC 1716–1729) are Christ’s self-portrait and the path to happiness.
talk: How do they differ from culture?
quiz: The Beatitudes are the path to…|Power|Fame|Wealth|Happiness|3|CCC 1720.
Blessed are the pure in heart for they shall…|See God|Be satisfied|Be comforted|Inherit land|0|Matthew 5:8.
Beatitude means…|Rest|Law|Fear|Blessedness|3|CCC 1716.
lessons.life: Memorize the Beatitudes.
lessons.saint: Francis and Clare: friends who founded the Franciscans and Poor Clares and lived the Beatitudes in poverty.
misc: The Beatitudes are for saints only.

lessons.title: Fulfilling the Law
lessons.idea: Jesus fulfills the Law with love.
lessons.question: What does “you have heard…” mean?
teach: Jesus fulfills the Law (Mt 5:17–48; CCC 577–582; 1967–1968). “You have heard… but I say.”
Interior obedience: anger, lust, oaths, love of enemies.
talk: What is different in Jesus’s teaching?
quiz: Jesus came to…|Ignore it|Abolish the Law|Amend it slightly|Fulfill the Law|3|Matthew 5:17.
“Love your enemies” is…|Part of the Sermon on the Mount|From Proverbs|Optional|From Exodus|0|Matthew 5:44.
The new law is written…|In books only|In the air|On hearts|On stone|2|CCC 1966.
lessons.life: Pray for someone who has hurt you.
lessons.saint: Stephen: the first martyr, who forgave those who stoned him.

lessons.title: Prayer, almsgiving, fasting
lessons.idea: Do not show off; seek God in secret.
lessons.question: Why in secret?
teach: Almsgiving, prayer, fasting (Mt 6:1–18; CCC 1434–1438; 2608). Practiced in secret.
The Lord’s Prayer sits in the middle.
quiz: Jesus teaches to pray…|Never|On street corners|Loudly|In secret|3|Matthew 6:6.
The three works are…|Read, write, speak|Faith, hope, love|Prayer, fasting, almsgiving|Work, rest, play|2|Matthew 6.
The Our Father is found in…|Acts 2|John 3|Matthew 6|Mark 1|2|Matthew 6:9.
lessons.life: Plan a concrete Lenten practice.
lessons.saint: Francis: who gave up wealth to follow Christ in poverty and joy and loved creation.

lessons.title: Entering Jerusalem and the Last Supper
lessons.idea: Jesus gives himself.
lessons.question: What do these events show?
teach: Entry into Jerusalem and the Last Supper (CCC 557–560; 1337–1340): Jesus gives himself in the Eucharist.
talk: What did Jesus do at the Last Supper?
How is the Eucharist both meal and sacrifice?
quiz: At the Last Supper Jesus gave…|His Body and Blood|A sign only|A parable|A sermon|0|Luke 22:19.
On Palm Sunday he rode…|A horse|A camel|A chariot|A donkey|3|Matthew 21.
“Do this in memory of me” establishes…|The Eucharist|Marriage|Ashes|Baptism|0|CCC 1341.
lessons.life: Read the Last Supper accounts side by side.
lessons.saint: Thomas Aquinas: the Dominican friar who wrote the Summa Theologiae and hymns for the Eucharist.
misc: The Last Supper is only a symbol.

lessons.title: Gethsemane, trial, cross
lessons.idea: Jesus freely lays down his life.
lessons.question: Who is responsible?
teach: Gethsemane, trial, crucifixion (CCC 571–618): Jesus freely lays down his life.
Responsibility: all sinners (CCC 598), not the Jewish people.
talk: What do we learn from his words?
quiz: Jesus prayed in…|Gethsemane|Capernaum|Cana|Bethany|0|Luke 22:39-46.
His death was…|Accidental|A defeat|Unplanned|Freely accepted|3|CCC 609.
All sinners…|Are innocent|Share responsibility|Cannot be forgiven|Don’t matter|1|CCC 598.
lessons.life: Read the Passion in Luke.
lessons.saint: Veronica: tradition says she wiped the face of Jesus on the way to Calvary.

lessons.title: Why the Cross?
lessons.idea: The cross saves.
lessons.question: How does the Cross save?
teach: Why the Cross? Redemption, ransom, expiation, satisfaction, love (CCC 599–618; 1 Pet 2:24).
talk: How does the Cross shape our lives?
quiz: The Cross reveals…|God’s love|Roman law|God’s anger|Human power|0|CCC 604.
Christ died…|By accident|To impress|To scare us|For our sins|3|CCC 601.
“By his wounds we are…”|Healed|Warned|Led|Hurt|0|1 Peter 2:24.
lessons.life: Make the Sign of the Cross reverently.
lessons.saint: Paul of the Cross: a priest who preached the Passion of Christ and founded the Passionists.

lessons.title: The empty tomb and appearances
lessons.idea: Jesus rose bodily.
lessons.question: What proof?
teach: The Resurrection accounts (CCC 639–647): empty tomb, appearances, bodily resurrection.
Apologetic evidence: women as first witnesses, transformation of disciples.
quiz: The first witnesses were…|Priests|Women|Soldiers|Kings|1|John 20:1.
The risen Jesus…|Appeared to many|Was a dream|Appeared to none|Was a ghost|0|1 Corinthians 15:5-8.
The Resurrection is…|Symbolic|Bodily|Spiritual only|Imaginary|1|CCC 645.
lessons.life: Read the four Resurrection accounts.
lessons.saint: Mary Magdalene: the first to see the risen Lord and to tell the apostles.

lessons.title: The meaning of the Resurrection
lessons.idea: It confirms Christ’s divinity and promises our resurrection.
lessons.question: Why central?
teach: Meaning (CCC 651–655): it confirms Christ’s divinity and his teaching, accomplishes our justification and gives new life, and promises our resurrection.
talk: Why does Paul say faith is futile without it?
quiz: Without the Resurrection, faith is…|Still strong|Futile|Easy|Fine|1|1 Corinthians 15:14.
Christ is the…|Firstfruits|Last|Forgotten|Middle|0|1 Corinthians 15:20.
The Resurrection gives us…|Power|New life|Fame|Wealth|1|Romans 6:4.
lessons.life: Celebrate Sunday as little Easter.
lessons.saint: Paul: once a persecutor, he met Christ on the road to Damascus and became the apostle to the Gentiles.

lessons.title: Ascension and Pentecost
lessons.idea: Jesus ascends and sends the Spirit.
lessons.question: What happens next?
teach: Ascension and Pentecost (CCC 659–667; 731–732): Christ enthroned, Spirit poured out.
quiz: Jesus ascended…|Immediately|Forty days after Easter|On Good Friday|At Christmas|1|Acts 1:3.
Pentecost is…|Fifty days after Easter|Ten|Forty|Seven|0|Acts 2.
The Spirit empowers…|Fear|Revenge|Witness|Hiding|2|Acts 1:8.
lessons.life: Pray for the gift of the Spirit.
lessons.saint: Peter: a fisherman who denied Jesus and was forgiven, and became the first pope.
misc: The Ascension is a space trip.

lessons.title: Life in the first community
lessons.idea: They shared prayer, teaching and goods.
lessons.question: What marked them?
teach: The first community (Acts 2:42–47; CCC 949, 2624): teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread, prayers.
quiz: The early Christians devoted themselves to…|Teaching, fellowship, bread, prayer|Wealth|War|Politics|0|Acts 2:42.
They shared…|Their goods|Only prayers|Nothing|Their houses only|0|Acts 2:44-45.
Koinonia means…|Competition|Communion|Commerce|Control|1|CCC 949.
lessons.life: Do something with the parish this month.
lessons.saint: Barnabas: the “son of encouragement,” who welcomed Paul and traveled with him.

lessons.title: Peter and Paul
lessons.idea: Peter leads; Paul brings the Gospel to the Gentiles.
lessons.question: How did the Gospel spread?
teach: Peter and Paul (Acts 9–12; CCC 551–553; 849–856). Paul’s conversion and journeys.
quiz: Paul met Christ on the road to…|Antioch|Jerusalem|Rome|Damascus|3|Acts 9.
Peter first preached to Gentiles in…|Rome|Caesarea|Athens|Corinth|1|Acts 10.
Paul’s mission was to the…|Soldiers|Priests|Gentiles|Romans only|2|Galatians 2:8.
lessons.life: Map Paul’s journeys.
lessons.saint: Paul: once a persecutor, he met Christ on the road to Damascus and became the apostle to the Gentiles.

lessons.title: The Council of Jerusalem
lessons.idea: The Church settles questions together.
lessons.question: Who decides?
teach: Council of Jerusalem (Acts 15; CCC 865, 880–892): the apostles decide together; the Church resolves doctrinal questions.
quiz: The first council was in…|Ephesus|Nicaea|Jerusalem|Rome|2|Acts 15.
The decision concerned…|The calendar|Gentile converts|Music|Taxes|1|Acts 15:19.
It said, “It seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to…”|Paul|Rome|The king|Us|3|Acts 15:28.
lessons.life: Read Acts 15.
lessons.saint: James: an apostle and leader of the Church in Jerusalem, who taught that faith must be lived.
misc: The early Church had no authority.

lessons.title: Paul’s letters
lessons.idea: Paul explains faith in Christ.
lessons.question: What is justification?
teach: Paul’s letters (Rom 5–8): justification by grace through faith (CCC 1987–2029). Faith working through love.
talk: How do faith and works relate?
quiz: Justification is…|Feeling good|Earning salvation|A law|Being made righteous by grace|3|CCC 1989.
Faith works through…|Money|Love|Fear|Pride|1|Galatians 5:6.
Nothing can separate us from…|Death|Debt|The love of Christ|Sin|2|Romans 8:39.
lessons.life: Memorize Romans 8:38–39.
lessons.saint: Paul: once a persecutor, he met Christ on the road to Damascus and became the apostle to the Gentiles.

lessons.title: Living the Christian life
lessons.idea: The letters teach moral life and unity.
lessons.question: What are the “clothes” of a Christian?
teach: Christian life in the letters (Col 3:12–17; Eph 4–6): put on compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, patience, love.
talk: What does it mean to “put on” Christ?
quiz: Put on…|Pride|Compassion|Anger|Envy|1|Colossians 3:12.
Above all, put on…|Love|Silence|Fear|Money|0|Colossians 3:14.
Do everything in the name of…|Rome|The world|The Lord Jesus|Self|2|Colossians 3:17.
lessons.life: Choose one virtue from Colossians 3 each day.
lessons.saint: Timothy: Paul’s young co-worker, who led churches despite being young.

lessons.title: Revelation: hope for the end
lessons.idea: Christ will return and God will make all things new.
lessons.question: What is the message of hope?
teach: Revelation (CCC 1042–1060): the book unveils Christ’s victory and the new creation; liturgical vision.
quiz: Revelation ends with…|Judgment only|Defeat|Silence|New Jerusalem|3|Revelation 21.
Its main message is…|Christ wins|Doom|Fear|Politics|0|CCC 1042.
“Behold, I make all things…”|New|Lost|Old|Dark|0|Revelation 21:5.
lessons.life: Read Revelation 21–22 aloud.
lessons.saint: John: the beloved disciple, who stood at the cross and wrote a Gospel and Revelation.
